description: From linuxmusterDEV/templates/renovate.json (supply chain, stage A) plus what squid adds: the digest-pinned data-plane image and the hash-pinned Python lock files. Everything arrives as a reviewable PR; nothing is automerged.

pip-compile.description: The hash-pinned lock files packaging/build-venv.sh installs from. Renovate re-runs the uv command recorded in each lock's header (packaging/lock-deps.sh writes it), so the hashes are regenerated together with the pins. pyproject.toml leaves most dependencies unconstrained, so the weekly refresh (this manager's lockFileMaintenance, one PR for both locks) is what moves them; its schedule is open because the Renovate workflow itself only runs weekly (the default 'before 4am on monday' never matches the 04:00 UTC cron).

customManagers.description: Build image pinned as <image>:<tag>@sha256:<digest> in the workflows (IMG_LMN73/IMG_LMN74 in ci.yml and release.yml). The captured tag tells Renovate which tag's digest to follow.
The Renovate engine itself, pinned as RENOVATE_VERSION: <version>@sha256:<digest> in renovate.yml (validation and run use the same line; the action's default engine is too old for this config).

Pinned CI gate tools that ci.yml installs with `pip install tool==x.y.z` in the fast tier, so a linter widening its default rules cannot turn CI red on its own (uv compiles and checks the lock files).

packageRules.description: Data-plane image: pin + update by immutable digest. A human MUST merge (never auto-apply to a school's proxy).

PyPI releases (CI gate tools, lock dependencies) are proposed only once they are 7 days old, the window in which a compromised upload is usually still unnoticed. PyPI only: ghcr.io has no release timestamps, a docker rule would hold those updates back forever without a word (the Thursday schedule is the brake there). The weekly lock refresh gets the same age from --exclude-newer=P7D in the lock header.
Build image: never change the tag (24.04 -> 26.04 would be a new linuxmuster line, not an update), only follow its digest.
Build image digests in one PR, so ci.yml and release.yml always build with the same image. A human reviews and merges it.
Actions stay pinned by commit SHA with a # vN comment; a human merges every bump.
setup-python mirrors the target Ubuntu's Python (3.12 on 24.04 for lmn73); it changes with the linuxmuster line, not with Python releases.
Runners stay on the Ubuntu of the linuxmuster line (ubuntu-24.04 for lmn73): the install and upgrade smokes must run where the package is installed.
The Ubuntu base of the data-plane and test images follows the linuxmuster line too (24.04 for lmn73): new digests yes, a new release (26.04) only by hand.
Renovate engine: one PR that moves along until it is merged.

The github-actions manager reads renovate-version natively; it now holds ${{ env.RENOVATE_VERSION }}, and the regex manager above owns the engine. Kept off so a later literal value cannot be bumped twice.
